To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
daily intake of a standardized catechin mixture containing EGCG at 400 mg for 1 year did not reduce the risk of developing prostate cancer in men at increased risk for the disease.

daily consumption of 400 mg of green tea catechines (EGCG) in a decaffeinated formulation for 1 year did not prevent prostate cancer in men who had HGPIN or atypical small acini proliferation (ASAP) at baseline.

(i) daily consumption of green tea catechines for 12 months did not reduce the rate of prostate cancer among men with HGIN or ASAP; (ii) there was a significant reduction in the number of men with ASAP on the green tea catechine arm compared with the placebo; and (iii) the green tea catechin arm had a significant reduction in PSA.

green tea catechin intake at 400 mg EGCC per day did not reduce the rate of prostate cancer in a population of high risk men with high grade prostatic intraepethelial neoplasias and/or atypical prostate glands.
